\chapter{Complexity — P Closure}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PClosure
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module establishes the closure properties of the class $\mathsf{P}$ [AB09, Def.~1.13]
that are used tacitly throughout [AB09]: a language is in $\mathsf{P}$ exactly when its
one-bit indicator is polynomial-time computable, and $\mathsf{P}$ is closed under
polynomial-time preimages (many-one reductions), under intersection and union, and hence
under arbitrary Boolean functions of finitely many tests. As applications, comparing the
lengths of the two components of a pair, or of the outputs of two polynomial-time
functions, is decidable in polynomial time.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time decidability and indicator computation]
\lean{Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable}
\label{Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.mem_P_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{3}
For a language $V$ of finite binary strings, $V$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$ if and only if
the function that maps each binary string $x$ to the one-bit string containing $1$ when
$x\in V$ and $0$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time preimage closure]
\lean{Complexity.preimage_mem_P}
\label{Complexity.preimage_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable}
\difficulty{1}
Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $g$ be a polynomial-time computable
function from binary strings to binary strings. Then the language $\{x:g(x)\in V\}$
belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time tests define languages in P]
\lean{Complexity.mem_P_of_test}
\label{Complexity.mem_P_of_test}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $b$ be a Boolean-valued function on finite binary strings. If the function sending
each string $z$ to the one-bit word $[b(z)]$ is polynomial-time computable, then the
language of strings $z$ for which $b(z)=1$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-Time Computability of a Language Indicator]
\lean{Complexity.test_of_mem_P}
\label{Complexity.test_of_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $L$ be a language of binary strings. If $L$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$, then the
function sending each binary string $z$ to the one-bit word indicating whether $z\in L$
is polynomial-time computable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time closure under finite Boolean combinations]
\lean{Complexity.mem_P_of_atoms}
\label{Complexity.mem_P_of_atoms}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.compl_mem_P, Complexity.empty_mem_P, Complexity.inter_mem_P, Complexity.union_mem_P, Complexity.univ_mem_P}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $b_i$ be a Boolean-valued function on finite binary
strings for each $i\in I$, and suppose the language of strings $z$ with $b_i(z)=1$
belongs to $\mathsf{P}$ for every $i$. For any Boolean function $F$ on assignments of
bits to $I$, the language of strings $z$ for which $F((b_i(z))_{i\in I})=1$ belongs to
$\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time closure under block search]
\lean{Complexity.mem_P_of_blockAny}
\label{Complexity.mem_P_of_blockAny}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.blockAt, Complexity.mem_P_of_test, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockAnyTest, Complexity.test_of_mem_P, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers. For a
binary string $z$, let $x$ be the first component of its encoded pair (or the empty
string if it does not parse as a pair), and let $y$ be the second component (or the
empty string if it does not parse). Set $B=a(|x|+1)^k$, and let the block at index $i$
be the length-$B$ segment of $y$ beginning at position $iB$, truncated if necessary.
Then the language of strings $z$ for which there exists an integer $i<a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$
such that the encoding of the pair consisting of $x$ and its block at index $i$ belongs
to $V$ is in $\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time closure under block majority]
\lean{Complexity.mem_P_of_blockMajority}
\label{Complexity.mem_P_of_blockMajority}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.blockAt, Complexity.mem_P_of_test, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockMajorityTest, Complexity.test_of_mem_P, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers. For each
binary string $z$, take $x$ to be the first component of its encoded pair, using the
empty string if parsing fails; let $y$ be the second component, also using the empty
string if parsing fails. Put $N=a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$, and partition the initial portion of
$y$ into length-$B$ blocks at positions $iB$, where $B=a(|x|+1)^k$; blocks shorter than
$B$ are allowed at the end. The language of strings $z$ for which strictly more than
half of the indices $i<N$ have the encoding of $(x,\text{block at }i)$ in $V$ belongs to
$\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time closure under block XOR search]
\lean{Complexity.mem_P_of_blockXorAny}
\label{Complexity.mem_P_of_blockXorAny}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.blockAt, Complexity.mem_P_of_test, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockXorAnyTest, Complexity.test_of_mem_P, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers. For a
binary string $w$, take the first component of its encoded pair as an outer string, then
take the first component of that string's encoded pair as $x$; when either parse fails,
use the empty string for the corresponding component. Let $y$ be the second component of
the outer pair, using the empty string if parsing fails, and set $B=a(|x|+1)^k$ and
$N=a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$. The language of strings $w$ for which some $i<N$ has the following
property belongs to $\mathsf{P}$: the encoding of the pair $(x,
y\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}_\ell u_i)$ is in $V$, where $u_i$ is the length-$B$ block of the
second component of the inner pair at position $iB$, truncated at the end, and
$\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}_\ell$ denotes bitwise XOR on corresponding positions up to the
shorter of the two strings.
\end{theorem}
